headline: From first launch to a ready teaching studio
overview: A fresh Yoga Quest install explains visual planning, offline Teach Mode, and local-first privacy before opening the native studio with a prepared class.

steps.title: Plan the class as an arc
steps.action: Launched Yoga Quest from a freshly cleared app container.
steps.description: The native onboarding opens with the product's visual class-planning model: build a sequence, shape its arc, then teach from it.
steps.screenshotAlt: Yoga Quest native onboarding introducing visual class planning on iPhone

steps.title: Teach with the next cue ready
steps.action: Tapped Continue on the first onboarding screen.
steps.description: The second native screen introduces Teach Mode as a glanceable class companion with the current pose, the next pose, and timing kept in view.
steps.screenshotAlt: Yoga Quest native onboarding explaining offline Teach Mode on iPhone

steps.title: A private studio starts on-device
steps.action: Tapped Continue on the Teach Mode screen.
steps.description: The final onboarding step makes the local-first model explicit: planning and teaching work without an account, with sync presented as optional.
steps.screenshotAlt: Yoga Quest native onboarding describing local-first privacy on iPhone

steps.title: The native studio opens ready to teach
steps.description: The app lands on the native Studio tab with a prepared class, a prominent Teach this class action, and bottom navigation to Library, Explore, Learn, and profile.
steps.screenshotAlt: Yoga Quest native studio home with a prepared class and Teach this class action

keyFeatures: Native studio home with a prepared class
note: Captured from a newly built Yoga Quest 1.0.1+12 app on an isolated iPhone 17 Pro simulator running iOS 27.0. The run cleared only that temporary simulator's app container. It did not exercise a physical device, account sync, or a store binary.
